draft.title: Thermochemical equations
card: A thermochemical equation is a balanced equation that also gives ΔH, the energy change, in kJ. It includes state symbols, such as (g) or (l), because the state affects the energy.
The ΔH value is for the amounts shown by the coefficients. For C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g), ΔH = -394 kJ mol⁻¹ means 394 kJ is released when 1 mol of carbon reacts.
If you multiply the coefficients, you multiply ΔH by the same factor. Twice the amounts give twice the energy change.
If the equation is reversed, ΔH keeps its size but changes sign. A reaction that releases 394 kJ one way absorbs 394 kJ the other way.
draft.remember: ΔH goes with the equation as written: scale the amounts and ΔH scales, reverse it and the sign flips.

a.q: 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(l) has ΔH = -572 kJ. What is ΔH for H2(g) + ½O2(g) → H2O(l)?
a.why: The coefficients are halved, so ΔH is halved to -286 kJ. Keeping -572 kJ is tempting, but it is the value for twice the amounts.
a.clue: Compare the amounts in the two equations.

b.q: CH4(g) + 2O2(g) → CO2(g) + 2H2O(l) has ΔH = -890 kJ. How much energy is absorbed when 2 mol of CO2(g) and 4 mol of H2O(l) react to form CH4(g) and O2(g)?
b.why: The reaction is the reverse of the given one, so the sign changes and the energy is absorbed. The amounts are double those in the equation, so the energy is 2 × 890 = 1780 kJ. The 890 kJ options forget to scale it.
b.clue: Check both the direction and the amounts compared with the equation.

problems.detail: The question asks 'How much energy is absorbed', which already tells students the direction. The two 'released' options can be ruled out from the wording alone, so the direction check that the clue and the why point to is not actually tested.

The first bullet gives the unit of ΔH as kJ, but the example uses kJ mol⁻¹ (the VCE convention), and the questions use plain kJ. Mixing units without saying how they relate may confuse students about which unit belongs with a thermochemical equation.

check.summary: The chemistry and the intended answers (-286 kJ; 1780 kJ absorbed) are correct. Question b's wording ('absorbed') gives away the direction, and the card mixes kJ and kJ mol⁻¹ for ΔH without explaining the link.

proposal.title: Thermochemical equations
card: A thermochemical equation is a balanced equation that also gives ΔH, the enthalpy change, in kJ mol⁻¹. It includes state symbols, such as (g) or (l), because the state affects the energy.
Here kJ mol⁻¹ means per mole of reaction as written, with the amounts shown by the coefficients. For C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g), ΔH = -394 kJ mol⁻¹, so 394 kJ is released when 1 mol of carbon reacts.
If you multiply the coefficients, you multiply ΔH by the same factor. An actual amount of energy, such as 788 kJ for 2 mol of carbon, is given in kJ.
If the equation is reversed, ΔH keeps its size but changes sign. A reaction that releases 394 kJ one way absorbs 394 kJ the other way.
proposal.remember: ΔH belongs to the equation as written: scale the amounts and ΔH scales, reverse it and the sign flips.
